questions.expected: It is slower and less used than email, and needs a phone line
questions.memo: Faxes are older technology — slower and less common than email, and they depend on a phone line.

questions.question: Sort each device by its main communication function.
questions.memo: Phones are for talking; fax machines, photocopiers and printers handle documents.

questions.question: A telephone call is an example of _________ communication.
questions.memo: A phone call is spoken, so it is verbal communication.

questions.question: Which is an example of written communication used for marketing in tourism?
options: A business's social-media posts and website
questions.expected: A business's social-media posts and website
questions.memo: Websites and social-media posts are written communication often used to market tourism products.

questions.question: True or false: A face-to-face conversation is a form of verbal communication.
questions.memo: Speaking with someone in person is verbal (spoken) communication.

questions.question: Why is good business communication etiquette important in tourism?
options: It creates a professional, friendly impression that satisfies customers
It is only needed when complaining
It has no effect on customers
questions.expected: It creates a professional, friendly impression that satisfies customers
questions.memo: Polite, professional communication makes customers feel valued and reflects well on the business.

questions.question: Match each communication tool to its main use.
questions.memo: SMS and instant messaging suit quick notes; emails, memos and vouchers suit formal records.

questions.question: Social networks such as Facebook are used by tourism businesses mainly to:
options: Communicate with and market to customers
questions.expected: Communicate with and market to customers
questions.memo: Social networks help businesses reach, communicate with and market to customers.

questions.question: What is the main function of a printer or photocopier in a tourism office?
options: To produce paper copies of documents such as itineraries and vouchers
questions.expected: To produce paper copies of documents such as itineraries and vouchers
questions.memo: Printers and photocopiers create paper copies of documents like itineraries, tickets and vouchers.

TOUR.G10.T4.SERVICE.A1.title: Service excellence
TOUR.G10.T4.SERVICE.A1.description: The concepts service and service excellence; the importance and value of quality service for a tourism business; the advantages of excellent service for the business and the tourist; the consequences of poor service; and recommendations for improvement.
TOUR.G10.T4.SERVICE.A1.recovery_strategy: Excellent service brings repeat business, good word-of-mouth and a strong reputation — it drives profit. Poor service loses customers and damages the brand.

questions.question: What is 'service excellence'?
options: Consistently meeting or exceeding customers' expectations
Serving as few customers as possible
questions.expected: Consistently meeting or exceeding customers' expectations
questions.memo: Service excellence means reliably giving customers service that meets or beats what they expect.

questions.question: Why is providing quality service important for a tourism business?
options: It builds a good reputation and encourages repeat business
It guarantees the business never makes a profit
It has no effect on the business
questions.expected: It builds a good reputation and encourages repeat business
questions.memo: Quality service keeps customers happy, builds reputation and brings them back.

questions.question: What is an advantage of excellent service FOR THE BUSINESS?
options: Loyal, returning customers and positive word-of-mouth
questions.expected: Loyal, returning customers and positive word-of-mouth
questions.memo: Excellent service earns loyalty and good recommendations, which grow the business.

questions.question: What is an advantage of excellent service FOR THE TOURIST?
options: A more enjoyable experience and good value for money
questions.expected: A more enjoyable experience and good value for money
questions.memo: Good service makes the tourist's experience more enjoyable and feels like better value.

questions.question: What is a likely consequence of POOR service delivery?
options: Lost customers and a damaged reputation
questions.expected: Lost customers and a damaged reputation
questions.memo: Poor service drives customers away and harms the business's reputation.

questions.question: True or false: Poor service has no effect on a business's profit.
questions.memo: Poor service loses customers and damages reputation, which reduces profit over time.

questions.question: Service that consistently meets or exceeds expectations is called service _________.
questions.memo: Service excellence = consistently meeting or beating expectations.

questions.question: Build the strongest argument for this thesis by selecting the strong points.
questions.thesis: Service excellence is good for a tourism business.

pool.text: Happy customers return and recommend the business to others
A strong reputation attracts new customers
It sets the business apart from competitors
Staff sometimes wear name badges
Hotels often have a reception desk

questions.memo: The strong points link service excellence to loyalty, reputation and competitive advantage. The red herrings are irrelevant facts.

questions.question: Compare these two guest reviews, then judge each statement.

source_a.text: Staff greeted us warmly, remembered our names, and sorted out our late check-out with a smile. We will definitely come back.
source_a.provenance: Online guest review of Lodge A

source_b.text: Reception ignored us, our room was not ready, and nobody apologised or offered to help. We won't return.
source_b.provenance: Online guest review of Lodge B

statements.text: Is a review of a place to stay
Mentions the price of the room

questions.memo: Review A shows service excellence (warm, helpful, memorable); Review B shows poor service (ignored, no apology). Both are accommodation reviews; neither mentions price.

questions.question: Which is a good recommendation for improving poor service?
options: Train staff properly and listen to customer feedback
questions.expected: Train staff properly and listen to customer feedback
questions.memo: Training staff and acting on feedback are practical ways to lift service quality.

questions.question: True or false: Good service encourages customers to return and recommend the business.
questions.memo: Satisfied customers come back and tell others, bringing repeat and new business.

questions.question: Sort each benefit by who it mainly helps.

items.text: A strong reputation and good reviews
Feeling valued and well looked after

questions.memo: For the business: loyalty, reputation, profit and competitive edge. For the tourist: enjoyment and feeling valued.

questions.question: Which is an example of excellent service?
options: A receptionist who greets guests warmly and solves problems quickly
A waiter who ignores customers for an hour
A guide who never answers questions
questions.expected: A receptionist who greets guests warmly and solves problems quickly
questions.memo: Excellent service is warm, attentive and quick to help.

questions.question: Which is an example of POOR service?
options: Staff who are rude and ignore a guest's request
A quick solution to a problem
questions.expected: Staff who are rude and ignore a guest's request
questions.memo: Rudeness and ignoring guests are clear signs of poor service.

questions.question: Unhappy customers often tell others, which can give a business a bad _________.
questions.memo: Negative word-of-mouth damages a business's reputation.

questions.question: True or false: Positive word-of-mouth from happy customers can attract new business.
questions.memo: Happy customers recommending a business bring in new customers — free, trusted advertising.

questions.question: Sort each behaviour as GOOD or POOR service.

items.text: Ignoring a guest who needs assistance
Apologising and fixing a mistake quickly
Being rude when a guest complains
Going the extra mile for a guest

questions.memo: Good service is attentive, polite and helpful; poor service is rude, dismissive or unhelpful.

questions.question: Why is service especially important in tourism?
options: Tourism is a people-based industry where the experience depends on how guests are treated
Because service has no link to the experience
Because products matter more than people in tourism
questions.expected: Tourism is a people-based industry where the experience depends on how guests are treated
questions.memo: Tourism sells experiences delivered by people, so the way guests are treated strongly shapes their satisfaction.

questions.question: A guest receives a cold meal. What is the best way to recover the situation?
options: Apologise sincerely and quickly replace the meal
Argue that the meal is fine
Blame the kitchen and do nothing
questions.expected: Apologise sincerely and quickly replace the meal
questions.memo: Service recovery means apologising and putting the problem right quickly, which can win back the guest.

questions.question: What is a likely consequence of CONSISTENTLY poor service over time?
options: The business loses customers and may eventually fail
questions.expected: The business loses customers and may eventually fail
questions.memo: Repeatedly poor service drives customers away and can lead the business to fail.
